name: PC Engine CD-ROM²
description: NEC's CD-ROM add-on for the PC Engine, released in Japan in 1988 and in North America as the TurboGrafx-CD. It was the first CD-ROM system for a home console, and its Red Book audio, voice acting and anime cutscenes defined games like Ys Book I & II.

specs.memory: 64 KB RAM (System Card), 256 KB with Super System Card; +2 MB with Arcade Card
specs.sound: HuC6280 wavetable + OKI MSM5205 ADPCM + CD audio

curiosities: The drive needs a 'System Card' HuCard in the console's slot, and later games required upgraded Super System or Arcade cards.
The 1994 Arcade Card added extra RAM so that Neo Geo fighting games such as Art of Fighting and Fatal Fury Special could be ported.
Ys Book I & II used CD audio and voiced, animated cutscenes years before most consoles had a CD drive.
The Super System Card of 1991 raised the drive's buffer RAM from 64 KB to 256 KB.
bestsellers: Akumajou Dracula X: Chi no Rondo
story: NEC and Hudson released the CD-ROM² for the PC Engine in December 1988, the first CD drive for a console.
CDs brought recorded music, voice and animated scenes to games such as Ys I & II, Gate of Thunder and Dracula X: Rondo of Blood.
Its upgrades, Super CD-ROM² and Arcade CD-ROM², kept it going in Japan for years.
